assessment_summary: The statement claims that a single Kempe-chain interchange is always sufficient to reduce the number of colors on the neighbors of a degree-5 vertex to at most three. This is false, and corresponds to the famous flaw in Alfred Kempe's 1879 proof of the Four Color Theorem (discovered by Percy Heawood in 1890). We can construct a simple planar graph and a valid 4-coloring of G-v where every possible single Kempe-chain interchange fails to eliminate any color from the neighborhood of v.
counterexample:
Graph G with vertices {v, v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, A, B, C, D}. 
Edges of G: 
- (v, vi) for i=1..5
- A cycle v1-v2-v3-v4-v5-v1
- A path v1-A-B-v3
- A path v1-C-D-v4

Planar embedding: Place v at the center and v1..v5 forming a convex pentagon around it. Draw the path v1-A-B-v3 entirely outside the pentagon on the right side. Draw the path v1-C-D-v4 entirely outside the pentagon on the left side. No edges cross, so G is a planar graph. Vertex v has degree 5.

Proper 4-coloring c of G-v: 
v1=1, v2=2, v3=3, v4=4, v5=2, A=3, B=1, C=4, D=1.
(One can easily verify that all edges in G-v connect vertices of different colors).

The neighbors of v (v1..v5) have colors 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 respectively, so all 4 colors appear.
Now we check all possible single Kempe-chain interchanges that involve the neighbors of v:
- 1-2 component containing v1,v2,v5: Swap changes v1->2, v2->1, v5->1. Neighbor colors become 2, 1, 3, 4, 1. (4 colors remain)
- 1-3 component containing v1,A,B,v3: Swap changes v1->3, v3->1. Neighbor colors become 3, 2, 1, 4, 2. (4 colors remain)
- 1-4 component containing v1,C,D,v4: Swap changes v1->4, v4->1. Neighbor colors become 4, 2, 3, 1, 2. (4 colors remain)
- 2-3 component containing v2,v3: Swap changes v2->3, v3->2. Neighbor colors become 1, 3, 2, 4, 2. (4 colors remain)
- 2-3 component containing v5: Swap changes v5->3. Neighbor colors become 1, 2, 3, 4, 3. (4 colors remain)
- 2-4 component containing v4,v5: Swap changes v4->2, v5->4. Neighbor colors become 1, 2, 3, 2, 4. (4 colors remain)
- 2-4 component containing v2: Swap changes v2->4. Neighbor colors become 1, 4, 3, 4, 2. (4 colors remain)
- 3-4 component containing v3,v4: Swap changes v3->4, v4->3. Neighbor colors become 1, 2, 4, 3, 2. (4 colors remain)

Since any other Kempe chain is disjoint from the neighborhood of v and would leave the neighbor colors entirely unchanged (leaving 4 colors), NO single Kempe-chain interchange leaves at most three colors on the neighbors of v. The statement is INVALID.
